questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the destination had a english speaking majority in order to make the socialisation easier.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learnt a lot both academically and personally and wouldn't have been without the experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very simple, there was good information and communication from the university, and you could easily get in touch with the office and lecturers if you had questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance when I arrived as it was not necessary

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation through the university, there was a very easy application portal and everything worked very easily. Even though I was out at the last minute, I was still able to get accommodation without having to apply for anything privately.  I can only recommend accommodation through the university as you get to socialise with other students you wouldn't have met otherwise.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There was no on-campus accommodation, but my accommodation was close to campus and I could walk in 15 minutes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to register for the courses, but a bit difficult because you couldn't see which courses were full, so you had to apply several times

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Courses were enrolled through the school's application portal with easy to follow templates and guides

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you had trouble finding courses, you could write to your assigned advisor at school

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of 3 of my first priorities because one of the courses was full, but I'm happy with the courses I ended up with

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply early to maximise your chances of getting the courses you want. And maybe take advantage of the fact that you can get 1st and 2nd semester courses approved, even if you're on your master's programme

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many interesting courses to choose from and it was great that you were not tied to a specific programme, but had the freedom to choose from other faculties

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3rd and 4th year undergraduate courses, but some of the people I spoke to also got 2nd year courses approved

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Classes are divided into smaller groups, for most of my courses there were around 40-50 people per class, so the teaching is more interactive and you are assessed on your active participation in class. But it's possible to do well in terms of active participation simply by participating in group discussions, you don't necessarily have to participate in plenary

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in 1) Social and Political Movements, 2) Populism: pathology or panacea?, and 3) Party politics and the welfare state

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend all the courses, but I found the populism course particularly educational and relevant and not a course I have had the opportunity to take at UCPH

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You should be aware that when you move in to your accomodation, everything is completely empty, meaning you have to buy your own pots, pans, plates, duvet, pillow etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices are almost the same as in Denmark, but you save a little on beer and coffee, especially as a student, simce there are often student deals on beer :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of societies available, there is definitely something for everyone!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was in the scandi society and a knitting society, which are highly recommended for socialising

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on several trips on weekends to visit some nice towns nearby. I went to Stirling, Glasgow and Newcastle, among others. I was also in London twice as it's only 4 hours by train. I can also only recommend going on a highland tour.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy! I found the locals to be very friendly and the culture is very similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly talked to other exchange students, but if you want to socialise with local students, there are plenty of opportunities to do so in the classes of the courses you are enrolled in

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked their pub culture, it made it easy to socialise on weekdays as you weren't necessarily too late for school the next day

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be open to all new experiences, even if it can be overwhelming at first
2) say yes to as much as possible, you'll regret it if you don't experience a lot
3) Prioritise the social over the academic! Take advantage of your grades being transferred as pass/fail

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring some personalised items to your room, it means a lot to feel at home and have some memories from home

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: definitely the socialising and the community you get with other fellow students. It's a very special experience and something you'll never experience again. It's hard to explain to others, but you get to live in a bubble where you only have to relate to the few people who are also away on exchange, all the things that take time at home don't take up your time when you're away, neither work, family, or other obligations

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the hardest part was missing home at first, but as time goes by, other things take over and you have to remember that everything is exactly as it was when you left when you get home... which is actually a bit difficult when you come home and feel like you've experienced a lot, while those around you don't understand how the last 5 months have offered a lot of experiences

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Prioritise keeping in touch with the friendships you've made through exchange! They are the only ones who can understand your experiences, thoughts and frustrations after you return home

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
